items.title: A member of the family is covered by the coset determined by its own certificate
items.author: Gilad Chase; Neta Dafni; Yuval Filmus; Nathan Lindzey
items.work: Uniqueness for 2-Intersecting Families of Permutations and Perfect Matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 568-572: for the characteristic function of a 2-intersecting family of permutations with common certificate size at most n minus two, each member implies that the whole family is covered by the coset determined by a minimal certificate for that member with one image fewer. The proof (source lines 573-577) takes a minimal certificate for the chosen member, forms the coset it determines with one image dropped, and then, for any other member of the family, invokes the representative lemma to find a representative whose certificate meets the first in exactly the intersection of the two; that intersection bound is precisely what forces the member into the coset. The statement records the covering and neither the choice of coset nor the use of the representative lemma.
